observed_data.raw_fields: Existing raw rows carry engine, n, rep, process_ns, inner_ns, result, pmc. They have no loader/bootstrap/admission/warmup duration fields.
observed_data.interpretation: The whole-process elapsed is concerning but is not pure startup. It includes two HIGH-count warmups as well as the measured call. Do not subtract approximate warmup/kernel medians to claim a measured startup duration. Independently aggregated medians are not a phase trace.

sources.fact: Routes ordinary versus nested drivers; creates owned scratch/cache and bubblewrap; runs image --load; waits and removes scratch before wrapper exits.

Line23 is one large generated form: pins are checked, helper/prelude/producer explicitly loaded, source preflight and producer-install called. Native registration cell is restored; nine fixed application mappings are registered and checked. Input construction/checking, timer calibration and warmups precede measured call; validation follows it.
Nested row loads its separate runtime-bootstrap, restores/registers two mappings, requires exactly two warmups, then separately times one n-count call and validates result.
Nested bootstrap contains three explicit loads (FXIR helper, full prelude, producer), expected source preflight, and producer-install, matching ordinary route preparation structure.

Preflight reads/hashes/parses module forms and checks definitions. Install preflights before helper initialization and again afterward, publishes candidates, recompiles each selected candidate for FX compiler admission and checks identities/providers. Helper initialization hashes helper+prelude and unconditionally calls load helper nil t (not require).

Only old-image hotpatch read/walk is guarded by absence of nelisp--fx-ir-table. That conditional walk is not proven to run on measured image. Subsequent helper defuns are outside that guard. Two explicit load requests therefore repeat helper definition processing on a successful standard source-loader route; do not call the conditional hotpatch walk unconditional work.

Registration is first-call deferred. register-prelude walks pending/early names, but is an explicit dump-time option; warm-for-dump selects all only when NELISP_FX_DUMP=all, otherwise a profile. Do not claim every prelude function compiles on every startup or that harness unconditionally calls register-prelude.

Normal --load conditionally evaluates embedded prelude only without valid cold image. Cold image restores globals and runs process-dependent reinit. Generic load reads/evaluates source; optional core/vendor wrapper may substitute compiled pieces but still processes load, with base-load fallback. No generic feature-based load-once guard is present on these inspected paths. Exact active loader interception on measured image was not dynamically traced.
process_ns brackets subprocess.run(timeout/taskset/engine-wrapper), including wrapper cleanup before return; inner_ns is parsed from driver-reported elapsed.
Loads core, resolves runtime linkage/handlers, passes argv and invokes initial Lisp function via main Lisp thread.
Core directory describes saved spaces; initial function and linkage addresses are read/adjusted from core entry.

Core saves global state; resumed start-lisp runs reinit then saved toplevel. This avoids reconstructing all initialized Lisp state from source, but does not eliminate per-process reinitialization or OS mapping cost.

design_inferences: Use general authenticated ready-state images or reusable admission artifacts to avoid repeating source reconstruction and admission work where exact module/compiler/ABI/closure/effect identities can be validated. Never skip required native evidence merely to lower time.
Keep process-dependent environment, signals, paths, FDs, clocks, thread and GC reinitialization explicit; saved state cannot safely freeze these wholesale.

Separate source boot, existing cold-image boot, authenticated application-ready image, and repeated work in one process. Require identical public loaded state and matching modules/ABI/compiler identities. Do not special-case benchmark functions.
Carry effect/root/snapshot contracts from Docs230-234; stale image/admission identity must reject or fall back without duplicate user initialization side effects.

proposed_timing_boundary_contract.epistemic_status: PROPOSED instrumentation; none of these new phase durations exist in current samples
boundaries: globals restored or embedded prelude complete
process exit and wrapper cleanup complete
proposed_timing_boundary_contract.rules: Monotonic timestamps in one clock domain where possible; tag run/image/module/compiler/ABI identity, count and nesting. Keep inclusive/exclusive intervals explicit. Record trace overhead separately. Never infer missing intervals by subtracting independent medians. Keep uninstrumented end-to-end process time as primary user-visible metric.
proposed_timing_boundary_contract.future_benchmark: Fresh alternating same-N processes with fixed CPU, same inputs, loaded public state and validation, predeclared warmups; compare source boot, validated cold image and validated application-ready image. Report image construction/admission cost, cache size and invalidation separately and in amortized totals; report cold/warm filesystem state as controlled or UNKNOWN, not assumed. Also report repeated calls within a process as a distinct cohort. Require stale-module/compiler/image negative controls and unchanged admission evidence.

unknowns: No phase durations; no numerical share of 7-10 seconds attributed to bootstrap/prelude/producer/GC/warmup/wrapper.
Actual companion cold-image acceptance for each historical process is not reconstructed from source alone.
Repeated helper load calls are source-observed; exact runtime loader specialization and CPU cost are not traced. Conditional old-image hotpatch walk may not execute.
Number of first-call compilations, retries, GC cycles and file-cache misses during preparation is not recorded by existing process_ns/inner_ns fields.
Source observations do not establish native/semantic qualification or performance improvement.
